🫁 #Technology available for #Licensing — we are looking for industry partners to scale up a novel immunomodulator in the #respiratory infection space.  

Developed and translated by the CCAMP translation research programme, Respi-Protect helps to prevent and treat respiratory infections such as the flu and COVID-19 through intranasal delivery.   

Respi-Protect's USP: A non-invasive, easily deliverable option for the prevention and treatment of various respiratory infections. 

What is the technology?
It is an immunomodulatory peptide-based immune-boosting mechanism with broad-spectrum activity against viruses like Influenza and potentially SARS-CoV-2  

How does it work?
Respi-Protect works by activating the innate immune system in the nasal mucosa, which is the initial entry point for respiratory pathogens. This activation is achieved by modulating the TLR2/4 pathways.

Studies conducted in animal models of influenza and COVID-19 have shown that Respi-Protect can be used both prophylactically and therapeutically, reducing lung damage and viral titers.

Partnering with IncuVateX to Build the Future of Incubation Management

We're excited to announce our partnership with IncuVateX (by YellowBerry Technologies Private Limited), formalized through an MoU, to bring IIT Mandi Catalyst's incubation operations onto one unified platform and to jointly build what it becomes next.

This isn't a tool we're simply adopting off the shelf and moving on. Our team will work closely with IncuVateX's product team to co-develop new capabilities shaped directly by how we actually run our programs, starting with what we roll out today and expanding steadily as our needs grow, our cohorts scale, and our reporting requirements get more demanding.

Why this partnership makes sense: IncuVateX brings a platform already built for compliance-heavy, publicly-funded programs. We bring years of hands-on experience running exactly that kind of program under real institutional and government reporting requirements. Putting those two things together means the platform evolves based on how incubation and skilling programs actually work on the ground the exceptions, the edge cases, the realities that don't quite match a generic template not how they look from the outside, on a whiteboard, in a product roadmap meeting.

It brings fragmented tools, manual workflows, and spreadsheets into one connected system, reducing duplication and turnaround time while providing a reliable, compliant, and audit-ready source of truth for founders and the incubation team.

For our founders of incubated startups, that translates into a faster, more transparent journey from wherever they enter our pipeline through to funding and beyond clear status at every stage, instead of chasing updates across channels. For our own team, it means far less time spent reconciling data by hand, and far more time actually spent mentoring the startups we exist to serve.

IIT Mandi Catalyst will also mentor IncuVateX’s evolution for PMKVY-style skilling programs, leveraging its experience in managing government-funded, compliance-driven initiatives to help build scalable solutions aligned with the real operational and reporting needs of skilling partners. 

This is the start of a long-term collaboration, not a one-time integration. As our programs grow and our skilling mandate expands, the platform grows with us  shaped jointly by the team that runs it day to day, for the institutions that will use it next. We'll be sharing more as the joint roadmap takes shape over the coming months.

What if carbon capture didn’t end with burying the carbon?

That’s the problem UrjanovaC Pvt Ltd is trying to solve. Founded in 2023 by Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay professors Vikram Vishal and ARNAB DUTTA, the Mumbai startup captures CO₂ from industrial exhaust and mineralises it into solid carbonate products.

Its modular system is designed to work with existing cement and steel plants, using industrial wastewater or seawater and earth-abundant materials in the process.

The company has raised about $1 million, and in 2025 was one of just three winners from 557 applications in the Avaana Capital–Startup India–NITI Aayog climate-tech challenge.

The bigger bet is simple: make carbon management something industries can pay for, not just a cost they have to absorb.

The final day of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program focused on building long-term scale engines - partnerships, investor readiness, and leadership evolution.

We began with “Channel & Partnerships: Designing a Partner Engine That Scales,” led by Venkat Shyam. Founders explored how structured channel #strategies, aligned incentives, and ecosystem #collaborations can unlock non-linear growth beyond direct sales.

In the #Fundraising Deep Dive: #Investor-Grade Company — From Pitch to Process & Metrics That Raise Money, Ravindra Krishnappa emphasized building companies that are investment-ready by design. The session broke down traction KPIs, investors' trust, #governance discipline, narrative clarity, and process maturity.

The program concluded with “Org & Leadership for Scaling: Founder-to-CEO Transition” led by Sathyanarayana B V, followed by final reflections and key takeaways. The conversation centered on building leadership depth, creating accountable org structures, and evolving from operator to strategic decision-maker. Sathyanarayana B V also spoke about #HR Management Grid, Leadership styles, how each one of them affects and has an impact in different workplaces, and how leaders are born or lost under different #leadership style

Scaling a startup ultimately requires more than #strategy - it demands founder transformation.

We thank all our expert #mentors and participating #founders for making this acceleration journey deeply insightful and impact-driven. At DERBI Foundation, our commitment remains clear: enabling startups with the right #ecosystem, right #frameworks, and right #mentorship to scale sustainably.

Day 2 | Expanding Markets, Strengthening Financial Foundations

Day 2 of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program shifted the lens from internal readiness to external expansion and financial resilience.

The day opened with “Market Access Strategy: #IndiaExpansion + Global Entry Readiness” led by Shivi Jain. Startups explored structured approaches to entering new markets, from regulatory preparedness and localization strategy to channel partnerships and #global positioning. The focus was on building scalable access, not opportunistic expansion.

In the Cashflow & Working Capital War-Room: Scale Without Dying, Nayak guided founders through one of the most underestimated growth levers — liquidity discipline. Through real-world scenarios and financial stress-testing frameworks, startups examined burn cycles, receivables management, and #capital efficiency as core survival metrics.

The day concluded with “Deal Structuring & Term Sheet Masterclass: Don’t Lose the Company” by Sharath Shyamasunder, The Startup Zone, where founders unpacked #investor clauses, dilution mechanics, control rights, and long-term implications of #fundraising decisions.

Growth is exciting. But #sustainable scale is built on informed expansion, disciplined capital management, and smart deal-making.
